title: Florida's 8th Congressional District 2026 General Election
description: The 2026 race for Florida's 8th Congressional District features Republican incumbent Mike Haridopolos, who was first elected in 2024, facing Democratic challenger Jennifer Jenkins, a former Brevard County School Board member. The district, which covers the Space Coast including Brevard County and parts of Orange County, was redrawn in 2026 and leans Republican with a Cook PVI of R+8. Haridopolos holds a significant fundraising advantage, while Jenkins emphasizes her local roots and experience fighting for public education. The primary election is scheduled for August 18, 2026, with the general election on November 3, 2026.

candidates.name: Mike Haridopolos
candidates.summary: Mike Haridopolos is the Republican incumbent U.S. Representative for Florida's 8th Congressional District, having assumed office on January 3, 2025. He previously served in the Florida Senate from 2003 to 2012, including as Senate President from 2010 to 2012. Haridopolos won his first congressional term in 2024 with 62.25% of the vote and has raised over $1.25 million for his 2026 re-election campaign.

candidates.name: Jennifer Jenkins
candidates.summary: Jennifer Jenkins is the Democratic nominee for Florida's 8th Congressional District. She previously served on the Brevard County School Board from 2020 to 2024, where she unseated incumbent Tina Descovich, a co-founder of Moms for Liberty. Jenkins initially ran for U.S. Senate in 2024, then switched to challenge Rep. Randy Fine in Florida's 6th District, before ultimately qualifying for the redrawn 8th District where she resides. She has raised over $565,000 this cycle with approximately $251,000 cash on hand as of Q1 2026.

forecast.rationale: No public polling exists in the race data, so this forecast is based on fundamentals. The district has a Cook PVI of R+8 and the Republican incumbent won 62.25% in 2024. Haridopolos holds a significant fundraising advantage ($1.25M+ raised vs. $565K for Jenkins). Jennifer Jenkins is a credible Democratic challenger with local name recognition from the Brevard County School Board, and the district was redrawn in 2026, adding some uncertainty. The primary election is still two months away (Aug 18, 2026), though both major party candidates appear set. Fundamentals point to a clear Republican advantage, but the lack of polling and district redistricting caution against a stronger rating.
